title: Keep public copy within its visual frame

verify.note: In-process actual pricing callback consequences extracted from the component, plus supplemental canonical CSS and source-owner bindings. Actual SSR, unchanged BlockRender snapshots and deployment browser checks are separate gates; this probe does not claim rendered-pixel proof. The probe also reads the actual browser connection policy and requires only the configured Sentry organization ingest origin; the exact deployment smoke suite remains a separate gate.

detail: Daniel requested every rewritten block fit visually and required a fresh final sweep. Final public preview checks exposed intrinsic-width overflow in narrow audience steps and a pricing ResizeObserver feedback loop with two stable mobile illustration sizes. Existing Frequency primitives now contain the step grid and size the mobile illustration by available width; desktop sizing and all plan facts remain unchanged. Heading-only renderer bands retain their requested spacing and no longer introduce an unnecessary clipping boundary; local painted ink already fit before this change, so no local baseline ink-loss claim is made. The copy-fit suite separately records strictly bounded raster-map paint using the observed empty-alt tile contract, retaining failures for meaningful media, labels, controls and unverified geometry. No customer content, DAWN styling, prices or transaction behavior changes. Focused and exact-preview verification must pass before release. Readiness uses the same native IntersectionObserver configuration as SiteFx, including ancestor clips and percentage root margins, with the existing six-second failure bound. Expanded route measurements use an instant return to the top and the existing eight-second geometry settling bound. Negative controls retain failures for intersecting elements that never reveal and permanently clipped copy; no assertion or tolerance is relaxed. Revised verification passed three focused suites and 29 tests, including unchanged protected BlockRender snapshots. The Heading renderer now remains byte-identical to main; the Frequency-only CSS selector uses its existing sole centered wrapper, display heading and optional canonical eyebrow/kicker structure, excluding content and media bands. All 39 offline browser selector cases pass. The in-process probe consumed 2.14 seconds of whole-process CPU against the unchanged 4.5-second ceiling; three actual baseline regressions and four mutations are rejected. The failed first proposal and its CI evidence are preserved, not reclassified as passing. Isolated browser controls separately cover all six audience configurations at three widths, the pricing collapse/restoration regression, all eight plan states, bounded map paint and strict readiness negatives. These source-bound/offline proofs do not replace the exact deployment matrix. Follow-up source review found an independently reproducible reveal-queue UX issue: 37 intersecting entries could defer the last reveal by 6120ms. The actual SiteFx callback now caps queue delay at 1020ms while preserving ordinary 170ms cadence and reduced-motion/hash bypasses; eight focused actual-callback tests and mutation controls pass. This does not establish the cause of prior CI retries. The map checker now accepts only observed square 256/512 natural raster tiles rendered at 256px, with absent or exact presentation role; labels, semantic roles and wrapper roles remain failures. New public-only native-observer timeout diagnostics preserve the original six-second exception and avoid text/query values. Expanded offline browser controls passed: 24 map cases and both native-intersection controls, including the original permanently pending six-second rejection and its public diagnostic. The final four focused suites passed all 37 assertions, including unchanged renderer snapshots and actual SiteFx callback controls; the bounded strict copy-fit closure passed. These local checks do not replace the pending exact deployment matrix. A subsequent public smoke check exposed an inherited connection-policy mismatch: the configured browser error transport attempted its organization ingest endpoint, which connect-src omitted. This batch adds only that exact organization connection origin, preserving all other directives and the strict console-error check. Four focused policy/transport suites passed 18 assertions, and removal, unrelated-origin replacement and wildcard controls were rejected. The public baseline refresh was explicitly authorized by Daniel after difference review; generated screenshots and fingerprint records are tracked separately from authored paths. The earlier Home readiness failure remains preserved and unexplained; a later clean capture is not treated as its causal explanation. The next exact public run completed with 219 first-attempt passes and four retry passes: three Home reveal-readiness timeouts and one animated Weave snapshot difference. Those first-attempt failures remain recorded; retries do not establish their causes. CodeQL separately rejected substring-based URL checks in verification code and an implicit global observer-test-double constructor. Verification now parses hostnames and compares complete connection-source tokens, with malicious-origin controls; the test double declares the native constructor signature. Runtime connection policy and native observer behavior are unchanged by these verification corrections. New release checks remain required.
